title: SD-Turbo, 512x512, one step, WebNN / Core ML

image.role: UNet + one Euler step + TAESD decoder + RGBA pack

image.note: 1650 MiB. 655 constants at 8-byte-aligned offsets, monotonically increasing, so any chunking that respects a constant boundary works; the loader also stitches constants that straddle a chunk seam. The trailing 4 bytes are alignment padding.

text.note: 649 MiB. 281 constants; the largest single one is the [49408,1024] float16 token embedding at 101 MB.

tokenizer.parity: 12/12 against HuggingFace CLIPTokenizer, including the '!' added-token case (pad_token is '!', so a literal '!' is id 0 and never reaches BPE)

out.role: encoder_hidden_states; feeds the image graph on device

sample.note: This is `latent_scaled` in the workbench's reference set. The recipe is NHWC, the reference bins are NCHW [1,4,64,64]; the caller converts.

encoder_hidden_states.source: the text graph's `out`, bound as the SAME MLTensor - never read back to JS

latent_raw.source: unscaled latent = randn(seed) * sigma_0, converted NCHW -> NHWC
latent_raw.note: bound separately because the in-graph Euler step needs the unscaled latent: latent = latent_raw - sigma_0 * unet_out

out.role: RGBA-packed pixels: one int32 per pixel whose low bits are R | G<<8 | B<<16 | 0xFF000000
out.toImageData: new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(buffer), 512, 512) - a permanent view over the readback buffer, zero conversion

latent.role: the post-Euler latent; a debug output the recording carried along
latent.note: WebNN requires every declared graph output to be bound at dispatch. Allocate it non-readable; at 32 KB the cost is negligible. The 67.85 ms default configuration did not declare it.

scheduler.name: EulerDiscreteScheduler
scheduler.identity: latent_final = latent_raw - sigma_0 * unet_out; both pred_original_sample and prev_sample coincide at one step with s_churn = 0

chaining.contexts: ONE MLContext for both graphs. `navigator.ml.createContext({deviceType: 'gpu'})`, then assertCoreMLFingerprint().
pattern: 2. Bind it as the text graph's `out` AND as the image graph's `encoder_hidden_states`.
4. await readTensor(embedding)  -- a completion fence, not a transfer; the value stays on device
6. await readTensor(out, hostView)  -- 1 MB into a buffer you own, allocated once
chaining.cachingTheEmbedding: Re-running the same prompt skips steps 3 and 4 entirely: the embedding MLTensor still holds it. That is the ~60 ms cached number.
chaining.twoContexts: If the graphs are on different MLContexts (a text-on-npu experiment, say), the embedding must be read back and written across, which costs about 0.1 ms and, on the ANE, 2.7x the float16 error.

requirements.browser: Chrome 152+ with WebNN and the Core ML backend
requirements.profile: A real on-disk, non-incognito profile. Core ML is gated on !is_incognito; an off-the-record profile silently falls back to TFLite/XNNPACK on the CPU at roughly 50x the time.
requirements.memory: The image graph holds 1650 MiB of constants and builds in about 25 s. Chromium has no compiled-graph cache, so every page load pays that again.

buildTime.note: one-off per page load, not per generation
